---
title: "What I talk about when I talk about science"
---

I am a physicist who used to do a lot of machine learning until I got side tracked into biology.
Now I'm trying to bring my disparate parts together into some coherent (and updated) intellectual whole by following the advice of William Zinsser
in [*Writing to Learn*](https://www.harpercollins.com/products/writing-to-learn-william-zinsser).
This book (first pointed out to me by [Thore Graepel's excellent posts](https://thoregraepel.substack.com/p/introducing-patterns-of-thought)) makes the point that writing clearly about a subject is the best
way to learn it:
"Writing enables us to find out what we know—and what we don’t know—about whatever we’re trying to learn."
Hopefully by trying to write clearly to you all, I will figure these things out and we'll both learn something.


For code and research projects, see [GitHub](https://github.com/forrestsheldon).
